evidence.field: file summary, original-file link, provenance and licensing
evidence.text: The file page labels the image as 東 in oracle-script style, says it is a digitally created Inkscape vector, and cites several character databases as sources. It points to J14291 in the Chinese Etymology database for this picture and declares the SVG representation public domain. The page’s actual Original file link resolves to https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/ff/%E6%9D%B1-oracle.svg; the earlier proposed path using /0/0a/ was incorrect. The web reader could not fetch the direct SVG because of a cache miss, but the source page exposed the link.
evidence.title: File:東-oracle.svg

evidence.field: file summary, original-file link, provenance and licensing
evidence.text: The file page labels the image as 東 in Shang bronze script style and names 東父乙尊 (late Shang) in its source note. It cites Sinica, Chinese Etymology, CUHK, Chinese Text Project and Chinese Linguipedia. The SVG is an Inkscape vector redraw, not a photograph of the vessel or inscription, and its page declares the SVG representation public domain. The actual Original file link resolves to https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e9/%E6%9D%B1-bronze-shang.svg; the earlier proposed /7/7e/ path was incorrect. The web reader failed to fetch this direct SVG with a cache miss, while its source page was inspectable.
evidence.title: File:東-bronze-shang.svg

evidence.field: file summary, original-file link, provenance and licensing
evidence.text: The page describes an Inkscape vector redraw of 東 in Shuowen seal-script style and names several character databases as sources, including the S04417 image in Chinese Etymology. It is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph. The page links the original image at https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c7/%E6%9D%B1-seal.svg and identifies reuse as courtesy/permission and copyright from Richard Sears website © 2003. The previous /4/42/ candidate path was incorrect. The web reader rejected rendering the direct SVG as an unsupported image content type; the source page and direct-link target were inspected.
evidence.title: File:東-seal.svg

search_audit.query: Wikimedia Commons File 東 oracle.svg; Wikimedia Commons File 東 bronze shang.svg; Wikimedia Commons File 東 seal.svg
search_audit.outcome: Searched and inspected each Commons file page. The bronze page appeared directly in search results; opened oracle, bronze, and seal file pages. Their page-linked original file paths showed that all three acquisition paths previously supplied were wrong.

search_audit.query: Inspect actual original-file links on Commons file pages for 東 oracle, Shang bronze and Shuowen seal; verify direct SVG access outcomes
search_audit.outcome: Clicked the actual Original file links exposed by the pages. Oracle and bronze direct-file fetch attempts returned cache misses; seal returned an unsupported SVG content-type error. The source pages expose valid direct URLs and substantive file descriptions/licensing, so all three remain useful candidates for the harness to download and visually inspect.

gaps: Direct SVG fetching through the web reader failed for all three assets (cache misses for oracle and bronze, unsupported SVG content type for seal). The actual page-linked direct URLs were captured rather than guessed; downstream downloading and visual inspection remain necessary.

The file pages identify source databases and particular source-image identifiers, but the Commons vectors are modern redraws. They should not be described as photographs or as direct facsimiles of an excavated artifact.

items.period: Shang dynasty oracle-bone script tradition; exact specimen dating not supplied on Commons page
items.tradition: Oracle-bone script style; modern vector redraw
items.caption: A modern redraw of an oracle-script form of 東, cited to image J14291 in the Chinese Etymology database. Early Eastern readings are debated; this drawing represents a script form, not an artifact photograph.
items.alt: Black vector drawing of an early oracle-script form of 東 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Useful early-form candidate because its file page identifies oracle-script style, traces this representation to a named Chinese Etymology image, and documents public-domain reuse. It can be compared with later bronze and seal forms; no claim is made that every early occurrence depicts a bag.
items.rights: Public domain dedication stated on the Commons file page for this SVG representation.

items.period: Late Shang dynasty, as attributed in the Commons source note to 東父乙尊
items.tradition: Shang bronze inscription style; modern vector redraw
items.caption: A modern redraw of a Shang bronze-script form of 東, associated by the file page with the late-Shang 東父乙尊. The drawing is not a photograph of the vessel inscription.
items.alt: Black vector drawing of a Shang bronze-script form of 東 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Pairs an early bronze-style candidate with the oracle-style candidate and includes a named late-Shang source attribution. Commons explicitly marks the artwork as an Inkscape-created vector and public-domain representation.
items.rights: Public domain dedication stated on the Commons file page for this SVG representation.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script tradition (Eastern Han dictionary tradition); redraw uploaded in 2015
items.tradition: Seal script; modern Inkscape vector redraw
items.caption: A modern redraw of 東 in the seal-script style associated with Shuowen. It illustrates a later conventional form connected with the historical 日-and-木 explanation; it does not prove that interpretation is the graph’s earliest origin.
items.alt: Black vector drawing of 東 in seal-script style on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Shows a later form useful for comparison with the early script candidates and the historically influential Shuowen interpretation. The file page cites source databases and specifically identifies an S04417 source image; the reuse notice should be followed as stated there.
items.rights: Commons page states courtesy, permission and copyright from Richard Sears website © 2003; follow its reuse/permission notice rather than treating this asset as an unrestricted public-domain redraw.

limitations.text: These are modern vector redraws with source-page provenance, not ancient artifact photographs. The pages provide useful style and source attributions but the proposed graphics have not been visually inspected in this research step.

Direct image fetch through the web reader failed, although each source page exposed its exact original-file URL. Any subsequent acquisition failure should retain the logged access error; do not substitute guessed Wikimedia hash paths.
